items.text: Chinese companies are quickly advancing their autonomous vehicle (AV) technology. In China, 16,000 licenses were recently issued for testing driverless cars on 32,000 kilometers of roads. Some major Chinese AV companies, like Baidu and Pony.ai, have also been testing in the US, with over 2.5 million kilometers driven in California between 2017 and 2023. These tests help them gather valuable data to refine their vehicle software. However, in 2024, the US proposed restrictions on Chinese and Russian AVs due to security concerns, putting these operations at risk. The fear is that data collected by these Avs, like location patterns or images, could be used for surveillance or manipulated for cyberattacks. This cautious approach to AV technology contrasts with China’s more supportive policies aimed at making the country a global leader in new technologies. Whether these companies will continue testing in the US remains uncertain as both countries navigate these concerns. Difficult words: refine (to improve), surveillance (watching to gather information), navigate (to direct). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese companies are making advances in driverless car technology. In China, they issued 16,000 licenses to test autonomous vehicles on many roads. Big companies like Baidu and WeRide tested their cars in California and got valuable data to improve their technology. But in 2024, the US proposed a ban on Chinese and Russian AVs because of security. These driverless cars collect lots of information, such as places people go and even images of their surroundings. Some people worry that China could use this information somehow. In the US, safety comes first in testing driverless cars, but in China, it is not like that because China wants to become a leader in AV technology. The future of Chinese companies testing in the US is unclear because both countries work to balance development and safety. Difficult words: advance (progress), autonomous (working itself), valuable (very important), balance (to make different things equal or steady). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese companies are working hard to make autonomous cars. These cars do not have a driver. China already gives 16,000 licenses to test these cars on roads in China. Big companies like Baidu are testing also in the US. Their cars drive in California. They get information which helps make the cars better. But in 2024, the US says that Chinese cars should not be on US roads. China can get information from these cars, like where people go. They may use it in a bad way. The two countries have different ideas about autonomous cars. The US cares about safety . For China, safety is not so much important. They want to grow fast. We do not know for how long will the US let Chinese cars go on its roads. Difficult words: license (an official document which says that you can do something), safety (being safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A hoard of 2,584 silver pennies from the Norman Conquest period has been sold for 4.3 million pounds (5.5 million dollars), making it the highest-value treasure ever found in the UK. The South West Heritage Trust bought the coins from the Crown. The hoard was discovered in Somerset in 2019 by a group of metal detectorists , who will share the money with the landowner. One of the finders described it as a dream come true, comparing it to winning the lottery. The hoard includes coins from Harold II and William the Conqueror, with a much higher quantity of these coins than previously found. The process of determining the treasure’s value took nearly six years, partly due to delays caused by the pandemic. This discovery is significant because it adds to the historical knowledge of coinage from that era. The coins will eventually return to Somerset, where the discovery took place, and the metal detectorists hope to continue searching for more treasures. Difficult words: hoard (a large collection of something valuable), detectorist (a person who uses a metal detector to find objects underground), coinage (a set of coins). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2019, a group of metal detectorists found a hoard of 2,584 silver pennies from the time of the Norman Conquest. The South West Heritage Trust bought the coins for 4.3 million pounds (5.5 million dollars), making it the most valuable treasure ever found in the UK. The men discovered the coins in Somerset, and they will share the money with the landowner. One of the finders said it felt like winning the lottery. This hoard has many coins from King Harold II and William the Conqueror. The process to sell the treasure took almost six years, partly because of the pandemic. Now, the coins will return to Somerset. The finders hope to continue searching for more treasure in the future. Difficult words: detectorist (a person who uses a metal detector to find objects underground), hoard (a large amount of something), valuable (costing a lot of money), treasure (a lot of something expensive such as money, jewels, stones, or metals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of people finds 2,584 old silver coins in the ground. The coins come from the time of the Norman Conquest. The coins sell for 4.3 million pounds or 5.5 million dollars. It is the most valuable treasure in the UK. The people who find the coins use metal detectors in Somerset in 2019. They will give some money to the person who owns the land. One finder says that it is like winning the lottery. The coins are from the time of Harold II and William the Conqueror. After almost six years, the coins will go back to Somerset. The finders are excited to keep searching for more treasure. Difficult words: coin (metal money), valuable (costing a lot of money), treasure (a lot of something expensive such as money, jewels, stones, or metals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You may not like insects, but all of life on earth needs them to survive. Birds, fish and reptiles feed on insects, and if there are no insects, they die from hunger. As they die, predators which eat birds, fish and reptiles die, too, which leads to a mass extinction . Furthermore, insects pollinate most plants which means people cannot grow crops without them. Insects are very important, so it was a great shock when a report found that the mass of insects is falling by 2.5 per cent a year. If this continues, there will be 25% less insects in just 10 years. If that happens, all of life will be in terrible danger. There are two answers to why there are less and less insects. It is probably earth’s rising temperatures, as well as the use of chemicals in farming. Difficult words: mass extinction (the dying of many animals), pollinate (move from plant to plant so that the plant can make new plants), crops (a type of plant which people grow for food). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Insects are important because they are food for other animals, and they also pollinate plants. Without insects, many animals will die, and it will be hard for people to grow crops . There is a new study which says that the number of insects is falling. Every year, there are 2.5 per cent less insects. If this goes on, there will be 25% less insects in 10 years. This would be a big problem. People think that there are less insects because the planet is getting warmer. People also use chemicals in farming, so that can be a reason, too. Difficult words: insects (small animals like ants, bugs, bees or flies), pollinate (move from plant to plant so that the plant can make new plants), crops (a type of plant which people grow for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Insects are small animals like ants, bees, bugs or flies. They are very important. Many animals eat them. If there are no insects, bigger animals have nothing to eat. Insects also pollinate flowers. Without insects, plants cannot exist. Also, people cannot grow crops without insects. There is a new study. It is shocking. It says that insects are dying. There are 2.5 less insects every year. In 10 years, there can be 25% less insects. This would be very bad. People do not know why this is happening. However, they think that it is because the planet is getting warmer. Also, people use chemicals in farming. That can be a problem for the insects, too. Difficult words: pollinate (to move from plant to plant so that the plant can make new plants), crops (a type of plant which people grow for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sweden has built a fish tunnel to help species that are weaker swimmers, like perch and bream. For almost 380 years, these fish couldn’t migrate freely between Lake Malaren and the Baltic Sea. Now, the tunnel offers them a new path, which should increase biological diversity in the area. It was built in the new Slussen lock system in Stockholm, which separates the freshwater lake from the Baltic Sea. Fish like salmon can jump, but weaker swimming species have struggled in this environment. The tunnel mimics natural conditions by using stones found in archaeological digs, and a camera monitors the fish as they pass through. Interestingly, the tunnel has even attracted otters, though fences are in place to keep seals out. This new fish tunnel is part of a broader effort to improve the ecological balance in the region. The goal is to improve the fish population in Lake Malaren by introducing new species and promoting regrowth. Difficult words: biological diversity (variety of species), mimic (to imitate). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Sweden made a new fish tunnel for fish that are weaker swimmers. For almost 380 years, these fish couldn’t swim freely between Lake Malaren and the Baltic Sea. This new tunnel gives them a way to move, which will help make more types of fish live in the lake. The tunnel is part of the Slussen lock system in Stockholm. Fish like salmon can jump, but some other fish are not strong enough. The tunnel has stones, which makes it look natural . There is also a camera to watch the fish. Even otters got in the tunnel. The goal is to help fish grow in number and improve the environment in the lake. Difficult words: tunnel (a passage through something), lock (a part of a canal or river with gates), natural (what nature makes, rather than people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sweden has a new tunnel for fish. Some fish, like perch and bream, are not strong swimmers. For almost 380 years, they can not swim between Lake Malaren and the Baltic Sea. Now, the tunnel helps them swim between these waters. It is part of a new project in Stockholm. Strong fish like salmon can jump, but other fish cannot. The tunnel uses stones to look natural . A camera can watch the fish as they swim. Otters also use the tunnel. The goal is to help the fish grow in number and make the lake better for nature. Difficult words: tunnel (a long path under something), natural (when nature makes something, rather than people), otter (a water animal with four legs and dark brown fur). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Truong My Lan, a prominent Vietnamese businesswoman, was convicted of masterminding a large-scale fraud scheme involving over 12 billion dollars. She has been sentenced to death, but she is appealing. Her case has shaken Vietnam’s business community and is part of a broader anti-corruption campaign led by the communist government. Lan built her wealth in the 1980s by investing in property and founding a leading real estate company. She manipulated bank ownership laws and created fake companies to embezzle vast amounts of money from Saigon Commercial Bank. This case is also linked to Vietnam’s fast economic growth, which has received good and bad reactions. The anti-corruption campaign aims to attract foreign investment but has been criticized for targeting political opponents and slowing down government decisions. Despite these issues, Vietnam is still popular with foreign investors, but its future success depends on clearer rules and better management. Difficult words: mastermind (to plan and direct a difficult activity), embezzle (to steal money from a company or organization), anti-corruption campaign (activities that prevent or lessen dishonest behavior by people in power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Truong My Lan, a rich Vietnamese businesswoman is guilty of a large fraud worth over 12 billion dollars. She received a death sentence but is asking for a new trial. Her case shocked Vietnam’s business world. Lan started her business by buying cheap land in the 1980s and created a leading real estate company . Over time, she also took control of a bank and used fake companies to take out large loans. Vietnam’s government is trying to reduce corruption , but this is impacting business activities. Even with these problems, foreign companies like Apple and Samsung are still investing in Vietnam, making it an attractive country for business. But Vietnam needs clearer rules for its economy to grow. Difficult words: fraud (the crime of getting money by cheating on people), real estate company (a company which buys, sell, and develops land, homes, and other buildings), corruption (dishonest behavior by people in power). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Truong My Lan is a rich businesswoman from Vietnam. She steals over 12 billion dollars. She gets a death sentence . She is asking for a new trial . Lan starts buying cheap land in the 1980s. She starts a real estate company . Her company becomes the biggest company in Vietnam. Later, she takes money from a bank. She uses fake companies. Her case is part of Vietnam’s plan to stop corruption . It has a big impact on the country’s money. Some people are worried about business rules in Vietnam. But big companies like Samsung and Apple are still putting money into Vietnam. It is a good place for making products. Difficult words: death sentence (killing someone who commits a crime), trial (a formal meeting in a court), real estate company (a company which buys and sells land and buildings, corruption (when powerful people do bad things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korea’s spy agency has revealed that North Korea is sending troops to assist Russia in its war against Ukraine. The report comes after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed that up to 10,000 North Korean soldiers could soon join the conflict. According to South Korean intelligence, 1,500 North Korean soldiers have already been deployed to Russia’s Far East for training, with a final number potentially reaching 12,000. North Korea has also reportedly supplied Russia with vast amounts of military equipment since August 2023. Western intelligence has expressed growing concern about North Korea’s increasing involvement in the war. Some reports suggest that North Korean engineers have already been killed on the battlefield. Both North Korea and Russia have denied the allegations . South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol has called for a security meeting, urging the global community to address this evolving and potentially destabilizing situation. Difficult words: deploy (move troops or equipment into position for military action), allegation (a statement that someone has done something wrong or illegal, without giving proof), destabilize (to make someone or something lose power or control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

South Korea’s spy agency reported that North Korea is sending soldiers to help Russia in its war with Ukraine. The news comes after Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelensky said that up to 10,000 North Korean troops could join the conflict soon. According to South Korea, 1,500 soldiers already went to Russia. Also, since August 2023, North Korea sent over 13,000 containers with weapons to Russia. Western countries are becoming increasingly worried about North Korea’s involvement in the war. Both North Korea and Russia say that these things are not true. NATO didn’t confirm the news, but South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol called for countries to help deal with this dangerous situation. Difficult words: spy agency (an organization which finds out secret information about another organization or country), increasingly (more and more), involvement (taking part in something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korea says that North Korea is sending soldiers to help Russia fight in Ukraine. South Korea says that 1,500 North Korean soldiers are already in Russia. More could join soon. Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelensky thinks that up to 10,000 North Korean soldiers can go to Russia soon. North Korea is also sending guns to Russia. Western countries are worried about this. But Russia and North Korea deny it. NATO does not say yet what is happening. But South Korea’s president already asks for help from the international community to help with the situation. Difficult words: soldier (a person who fights in a war), deny (to say that something is not true), international community (the countries in the world considered as one group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Liam Payne, a former member of One Direction, has passed away at the age of 31. He died after falling from the third floor of a hotel in Argentina. Payne first gained fame on The X Factor in 2010 and became part of the famous boy band alongside Harry Styles, Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson, and Niall Horan. Payne’s struggled with mental health and spent a hundred days in rehab . Fans and fellow celebrities were shocked by the news of his death. His former bandmates, along with many others, paid tribute to him. Harry Styles’ mother, Anne Twist, posted a heartbroken message on social media. One Direction had a massive global impact, and Payne continued his music career after the group went on hiatus . His contributions to music and his legacy as a key member of one of the world’s biggest boy bands will be remembered. Difficult words: rehab (the process of helping someone to return to normal life after being ill, injured, or drug addicted), hiatus (a short pause in which nothing happens). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

One Direction singer Liam Payne died at the age of 31. He fell from a hotel in Argentina, as police reported. Liam was famous after being on The X Factor in 2010 and later became a member of the popular boy band with Harry Styles, Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson, and Niall Horan. Liam had problems with his mental health and alcohol, and he went to rehab before. Many people, including his friends and fans, are sad and shocked by his death. Harry Styles’ mom even shared a message online to show how heartbroken she is. One Direction became one of the biggest bands in the world, and after they paused, Liam worked on his music. Even after his death, fans will always remember him for his music and kind heart. Difficult words: mental (relating to the mind and thinking), rehab (a place where people go to get help when they have a problem with drugs), heartbroken (very sad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Liam Payne is a singer for the band One Direction. He dies at 31 years old. He falls from a hotel in Argentina. Liam becomes famous after he is on a TV show, The X Factor. He is in the band with Harry Styles, Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson, and Niall Horan. But it is not easy to be famous. Liam has some problems with drinking. He is in rehab to get help. One Direction is a very famous band. After they stop, Liam is still making music. Many people are very sad because of his death. His friends and fans share messages to show how much they miss him. Fans will remember him for his music and his kind personality . Difficult words: famous (when many people know someone), rehab (a place to get help when you take drugs), personality (how you are as a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three major tobacco companies Philip Morris, British American Tobacco, and Japan Tobacco have agreed to pay 23.6 billion dollars to settle a lawsuit in Canada. This lawsuit, which began in 2015, involves Canadian smokers and former smokers who accused the companies of failing to warn consumers about the health risks of smoking, despite knowing since the 1950s that cigarettes cause cancer. A Quebec court ruled in favor of the plaintiffs , awarding them 15 billion dollars, leading the companies to seek bankruptcy protection. Since 2019, their Canadian units have been negotiating the settlement under court supervision. Although the total settlement amount is confirmed, dividing the payment among the companies remains unresolved. Voting on the plan is expected in December 2024. British American Tobacco views the agreement as a positive step toward resolution , while Japan Tobacco hasn’t commented on the latest developments yet. Difficult words: plaintiff (a person who brings a case against another in a court of law), bankruptcy (a legal state when a person or company cannot pay its debts), resolution (solving a problem). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Three big cigarette companies Philip Morris, British American Tobacco, and Japan Tobacco will pay 23.6 billion dollars to end a lawsuit in Canada. The lawsuit started in 2015 when smokers and former smokers sued these companies, saying they didn’t warn people about the risks of smoking, even though they knew cigarettes caused cancer since the 1950s. A court in Quebec decided the companies had to pay 15 billion dollars. As a result, their Canadian branches had big problems with money. The companies started negotiating the final payment in 2019. They agreed on the total amount but it is unclear how they will divide the payment. The final vote on the plan should be in December 2024. Difficult words: lawsuit (a case in court between people or organizations), cancer (a disease when cells in a part of the body start to grow without control), divide (to separate into parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three cigarette companies, Philip Morris, British American Tobacco, and Japan Tobacco, will pay 23.6 billion dollars to end a big problem in Canada. People sue the companies. They do not tell people that smoking is dangerous. But since the 1950s, everybody knows that smoking causes cancer . A court in Quebec says that the companies must pay 15 billion dollars to smokers. Their Canadian offices ask for help. They do not have so much money. Since 2019, the companies are talking about how to pay. But they still do not know how to share the money between them. They will decide in December 2024. Difficult words: sue (to take someone to court), cancer (a disease when some parts of the body start to grow without control), share (to divide or give a part to others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A severe drought and wildfires in Brazil this year have once again demonstrated the destructive effects of climate change. These events have raised awareness of one of Brazil’s most prominent Indigenous activists, Ailton Krenak, who advocates for a renewed relationship with nature. Kraki, known as the philosopher of the forest, is a writer and journalist who fights for human rights and Indigenous rights in Brazil. Krenak’s family was forced to leave their land 50 years ago due to illegal logging . He warns that human activities are supporting environmental destruction. The wildfires are devastating Brazil and its vast Amazon forest. Some events are unpredictable; however, Kenak believes that human actions are significantly contributing to the problem. He also emphasizes the importance of history and Indigenous heritage. Without knowing where we come from, we cannot understand where we are going. Difficult words: awareness (knowing that something exists), prominent (important and famous), logging (cutting down trees), vast (extremely big). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This year, Brazil is facing a bad drought and wildfires, showing how climate change is affecting the world. These events are also making people more aware of Indigenous activist Ailton Krenak. He wants people to rethink their connection with nature. Krenak is a writer and journalist and he is known as the philosopher of the forest. He fights for the rights of Indigenous people in Brazil. Kraki’s family had to leave their land 50 years ago because of illegal logging . He warns that people are harming the environment. He says that while not everything happens as a result of climate change, people are making things worse. He also says that we need to remember history because, without it, we don’t understand who we are. Difficult words: drought (long time with no rain), rethink (to think about something again), logging (cutting down trees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year, there is little rain in Brazil. There are many fires. These events are making people listen to Indigenous activist Ailton Krenak. He wants people to think about nature. Krenak is a writer and journalist. People know him thanks to his books. They call him the philosopher of the forest. He fights for Indigenous people in Brazil. Krenak’s family must leave their land 50 years ago because of logging . He says that not everything happens because of climate change . But people are making things worse, like the fires in Brazil. Krenak believes that people must understand their past. Without it, they cannot understand themselves. Difficult words: activist (a person who fights for a change in politics or society), logging (cutting down trees), climate change (changes in usual weather because of the planet getting warmer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A severe drought in southern Africa is affecting millions of people, leading to a major food crisis, according to the United Nations (UN). Five countries – Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe – have declared national disasters as crops and livestock have been destroyed. Angola and Mozambique are also suffering. The UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) warns that the situation will worsen until the next harvest in March or April 2025. The WFP says over 27 million people are affected, including 21 million malnourished children. It is distributing food and cash to some areas but has only received one-fifth of the 369 million dollars it needs for relief. The drought, triggered by the El Niño weather phenomenon, has also led to electricity cuts and wildlife deaths in some countries. Urgent help is needed to prevent a full-scale humanitarian disaster. Difficult words: malnourished (not having enough nutrition), trigger (to cause an event or situation to happen or exist), humanitarian (related to saving human lives). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Southern Africa is experiencing a serious drought caused by the El Niño weather event, which makes some areas very dry. According to the United Nations, millions of people are without enough food. Governments declared a national disaster in five countries – Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. The drought is ruining crops and killing animals. Angola and Mozambique also have big problems. The UN says that more than 27 million people are suffering , and 21 million children are not getting enough food. The situation will get worse until the next harvest in March or April 2025. The UN is giving food and cash to people in need, but it needs a lot more. Difficult words: drought (long time with no rain), suffer (to experience something bad or difficult), harvest (getting crops and animals for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big drought is happening in southern Africa. Millions of people have no food. Five countries – Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe – are in trouble. No rain means that crops and animals are dying. Angola and Mozambique also have problems. The UN’s World Food Programme is giving food and cash to people. But it needs much more money. The UN says that 27 million people are hungry. 21 million children are not getting enough food. The drought will continue until March or April 2025. People will have new crops then. El Niño makes some places too dry. It is not possible to stop it. The UN needs 369 million dollars to help people in South Africa. Difficult words: drought (long time with no rain), crops (plants we grow for food), continue (to keep going or existing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In China, the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is nearly ready to start a significant experiment on neutrinos, mysterious subatomic particles. This 300-million-dollar project is located 700 meters underground in Guangdong province, and it will help scientists understand how neutrinos change and possibly reveal new information about the universe. Neutrinos are created by nuclear reactions and can pass through matter, including our bodies, without any effect. Studying them could explain important processes from the early universe. JUNO will observe neutrinos from nearby nuclear power plants and the sun. It may also study particles from Earth’s radioactive elements to help scientists understand the movement of tectonic plates. The project is expected to start in 2025 and will likely surpass the US-based Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), set to launch around 2030. However, funding issues in the US have delayed DUNE’s progress. JUNO aims to be a global leader in neutrino research, advancing both science and technology. Difficult words: subatomic (smaller than atoms), surpass (to be better than), advance (to develop or improve). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) in China will soon begin a big experiment to study neutrinos. Neutrinos are very small particles created by nuclear reactions. They can pass through things like the human body without any effect. JUNO will study how these particles change and what that can tell us about the universe. JUNO is located underground and costs 300 million dollars. It will get data from nearby nuclear power plants and may also study particles from the sun and the Earth. The project will start in 2025 and help scientists understand how Earth’s plates move. A similar US project called DUNE is having delays because of money problems. JUNO may become the world leader in this important area of research. Difficult words: experiment (a test which scientists do), data (information), particle (a small or the smallest amount of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China is building a lab called JUNO. Scientists will study small things called neutrinos there. Neutrinos exist in nuclear reactions. They can go through many things, even our bodies, and they do not change. Scientists will learn more about how neutrinos work. They can help us understand the universe . The lab is deep underground in China. It costs 300 million dollars. It will start in 2025. It will look at neutrinos from nuclear power plants and from the sun. This information will help us understand how the Earth’s surface moves. JUNO will be ready before a similar project in the US called DUNE. DUNE has problems with money. It will be ready around 2030. Difficult words: nuclear (connected to energy from atoms), universe (all existing things like stars, planets, galaxies, and so on), surface (the outside part of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Elon Musk revealed Tesla’s robotaxi, the Cybercab, at a major event in Los Angeles. The futuristic car has two gull-wing doors, no steering wheel or pedals, and will be priced under 30,000 dollars, with production starting in 2026. Musk also introduced a robovan that can carry 20 people. Tesla aims to become a robotics company rather than just a car manufacturer. Musk believes that fully autonomous cars could be ten times safer than human drivers, but he acknowledged that regulatory and safety challenges remain. Operating costs for the Cybercab will be around 20 cents per mile, while the robovan could be as low as 5 cents per mile. Tesla’s vehicles rely on AI and cameras instead of more common self-driving tech. Musk also mentioned progress on Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robot, expected to cost 20,000 to 30,000 dollars. However, analysts are skeptical about Tesla meeting its ambitious timelines, and some investors were disappointed by the lack of clear production details at the event. Difficult words: autonomous (self-driving), regulatory (related to laws and rules), skeptical (doubtful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Elon Musk showed off Tesla’s new robotaxi, the Cybercab, at a big event in Los Angeles. The Cybercab has no steering wheel or pedals, and it opens with two wing doors. It will cost less than 30,000 dollars, and production will start in 2026. Musk also revealed a robovan, which can carry up to 20 people. Tesla is now focusing more on robotics than just making cars. Musk believes these self-driving cars will be much safer than human drivers, but there are still problems with safety and laws. The Cybercab will cost 20 cents per mile to operate, while the robovan will cost only 5 cents per mile. Musk also talked about Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robot. But some investors were disappointed that there were not clear production details or timelines for the robotaxi. Difficult words: steering wheel (a part of a car to control where you are going), robotics (designing and operating of robots), humanoid (looking like a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Elon Musk shows Tesla’s new robotaxi, the Cybercab, in Los Angeles. The car has no steering wheel or pedals. It will cost less than 30,000 dollars. Production will begin in 2026. Musk also introduces a robovan. It can carry 20 people. Tesla is now focusing on making robots, not just cars. Musk says that these self-driving cars will be much safer than human drivers. But there are still problems with safety. The Cybercab will cost 20 cents per mile to use, and the robovan will cost only 5 cents per mile. Musk also talks about Tesla’s robot called Optimus. Some people are unhappy because Musk does not give much information about the robotaxi. Difficult words: steering wheel (a part of a car which you hold with your hands when you are driving), focus (to be the most interested in something), self-driving (a car with no driver). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Milton caused widespread destruction across Florida, killed at least 10 people, and left over 3.2 million homes and businesses without power. The hurricane weakened as it moved toward Florida’s east coast, avoiding the feared worst-case scenario , according to Governor Ron DeSantis. However, severe flooding and tornadoes were reported, with at least 27 tornadoes hitting the state. St. Lucie County suffered the most damage, with five deaths, including two in senior-living communities. The Tampa Bay area avoided the worst storm surge but experienced flooding on barrier islands. Residents shared terrifying stories, like Crystal Coleman, who feared for her life as a tornado ripped off her roof. Many homes were destroyed, and some areas were still recovering from Hurricane Helene two weeks earlier. Despite Milton weakening from a Category 5 to a Category 3 hurricane, it caused significant damage, especially from tornadoes and flooding. President Joe Biden emphasized the need for disaster relief funding. Difficult words: widespread (covering a large area), scenario (a possible situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hurricane Milton caused a lot of damage in Florida, killed at least 10 people, and left millions without power. The storm hit the west coast as a strong Category 3 hurricane but weakened as it moved to the east coast. Although Florida avoided the worst-case situation, many places experienced heavy flooding and tornadoes. Over 27 tornadoes touched down, and they killed five people in St. Lucie County. A US judge has ruled that rapper and producer Sean Diddy Combs will face trial in May 2025 on charges of sex trafficking and racketeering . Combs, who has pleaded not guilty, is accused of using his business empire to transport women and male sex workers across state lines for recorded sexual activities. If convicted, he could face a life sentence. Combs has been in jail for the last three weeks following raids on his homes in Miami and Los Angeles earlier this year. His mother, Janice, and other family members, including his daughters, were in court to support him. Combs’ lawyer has claimed the sexual activities were consensual and has requested a gag order to prevent evidence leaks to the media. Besides the criminal case, Combs is also facing several civil lawsuits from people accusing him of sexual misconduct. Prosecutors have hinted at more charges, which could further complicate his legal battle. Difficult words: racketeering (doing illegal business activities), consensual (with the willing agreement of all the people involved), gag order (an official order that prohibits the witnesses, lawyers, and other parties from discussing a legal case), hint (to suggest). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European Court of Justice has ruled that plant-based manufacturers can continue using meat-related names, such as “vegetarian burger” or “vegan steak.” This decision promotes consumer transparency but raises concerns about potential market fragmentation across Europe. The ruling has met mixed reactions from consumers. While some argue that plant-based products should have different names since they are not meat, others find familiar terms useful for recipes. In France, however, strict laws prevent plant-based items from using terms like “steak” or “ham,” creating uncertainty for producers. While the meat industry is not expected to be negatively affected, industry experts warn that different regulations in each country may lead to confusion. A survey shows that around 70% of consumers support using traditional meat names for plant-based items if the products are marked as vegetarian or vegan. Difficult words: consumer transparency (being open and honest to consumers in all aspects of the business), market fragmentation (dividing a marketplace into many small markets). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

About 70% of consumers are okay with using meat names if the product has a vegetarian or vegan label . Difficult words: plant-based (coming from plants, not animals), confuse (to make unclear or difficult to understand), current (the one which exists now), label (a small piece of paper or plastic which gives information about a product or object). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to US researchers Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun for discovering microRNA. They will share nearly a million euros. MicroRNA is a class of small molecules that play a vital role in regulating how genes are expressed, influencing the development of different types of cells in the body, such as muscles, neurons, and heart cells. Their discovery was made in the 1990s and initially focused on a worm species. However, by 2000, it was found that microRNA is also essential in humans. Although the award recognizes basic scientific research, there are no direct medical applications for it yet. The discovery is considered a significant advancement in understanding how genes are translated into proteins, but more research is needed to uncover its future benefits. Difficult words: vital (necessary, essential), application (putting something into use or operation), advancement (development or improvement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At first, scientists found microRNA in worms, but later, they learned it is also important in humans. The award is for basic science, so there are no clear uses in medicine right now. The discovery helps scientists understand better how genes turn into proteins, which may be useful in the future. Difficult words: tiny (very small), gene (a part of the DNA which controls how the body grows), discovery (finding something new). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China has introduced temporary anti-dumping measures on brandy imports from the EU, especially affecting famous French brands like Hennessy and Remy Martin. This comes after the EU voted to impose tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles (EVs). According to China’s commerce ministry, EU brandy imports have harmed Chinas domestic industry. France criticized the move, calling it unfair and against free trade principles, and plans to work with the European Commission to challenge it at the World Trade Organization. Additionally, China announced it is reviewing potential tariff increases on large-engine vehicles, which would heavily impact German manufacturers. These actions are seen as part of growing trade tensions between China and the EU, particularly targeting France, which has supported the new EV tariffs. Difficult words: anti-dumping (preventing cheap foreign goods from harming local businesses), challenge (to call to prove or justify something), tariff (a tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Thousands of protesters gathered in Budapest outside the offices of Hungary’s public media corporation, MTVA, to demand greater press freedom. The protest, organized by opposition leader Péter Magyar of the TISZA party, was directed against what critics call a ‘propaganda factory’ that serves the government. Magyar, who leads the most significant opposition to Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, said the public media spreads lies and distorts the truth. His party received nearly 30% of the vote in recent EU elections and is growing in popularity. Media watchdogs claim that Orbán’s party controls 80% of Hungary’s media market, threatening press freedom. Protesters like Balázs Tömpe and Ágnes Gera expressed anger over media bias and censorship. Magyar called for the resignation of the public media director and urged people to attend another protest on October 23 to continue the fight for media reform. Difficult words: distort (to give misleading or false information or impression), watchdog (an organization that guards against loss, theft, or undesirable practices), bias (supporting or opposing a particular person or thing unfairly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: media (the internet, magazines, TV, and so on), opposition (a group against those in power), quit (to leave a position, or to stop doing something). After over fifty years, the UK is returning the sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, following a historic agreement. Located in the Indian Ocean, Hagos Islands include Diego Garcia, a crucial US military base. The UK had kept control since Mauritius gained independence in 1968, even evicting over 1,000 residents to create the military base. The dispute lasted for years, going through courts and international bodies like the UN. Increasing pressure from these institutions and declining support, especially after Brexit, pushed the UK to negotiate the handover. Although Mauritius will control the islands, the US will continue using the base for 99 years. The evicted Chagossians may return, though living conditions on the islands are difficult. The deal is seen as a victory for anti-colonial movements and international law. Difficult words: sovereignty (the power to govern a country or area), evict (to force people to leave a place), dispute (a disagreement or argument). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: military base (a place where soldiers or the army stay), pressure (force), living conditions (the situation in which people live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spain’s first transgender soccer team has made its debut in a regional men’s league in Catalonia, a significant achievement in sports. Fenix FC consists entirely of transgender men and had previously only played friendly matches. Now, they are competing in the fifth division of a Catalan regional league after overcoming various administrative challenges to gain federated status. This is particularly important given the rise of transphobia , with 302 reported cases of violence or discrimination against LGBT individuals in Catalonia in 2023. Hugo Martinez, the team’s founder, started Fenix FC to provide a safe space for trans men to play soccer, inspired by his own negative experiences while transitioning. Although their first official match ended in a heavy 19-0 loss, the players emphasized that their right to play and feel safe is more important than winning. The Catalan Football Association confirmed that all players, regardless of gender, can participate in men’s leagues. Difficult words: debut (the first appearance), federated (set up as a single centralized unit), transphobia (fear or hate against transgender people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: transgender (someone whose gender doesn’t match their birth gender), discrimination (unfair treatment), aim (to point or direct at a target). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
